product.name: Acute
product.tagline: Local-first multi-agent engineering workbench — sandboxed file tools, streaming chat, sub-agent orchestration, approvals, and an embedded browser on a single desktop.

pillars.title: Coding pillar
pillars.summary: Streaming chat with tool calls, project indexing, command palette, approvals engine, notifications, web tools — daily-driver quality on a real codebase. The R42 deep audit scored editing-reliability and context management as the two weakest internals.

pillars.title: Agentic system pillar
pillars.summary: Multi-turn agentic continuation + owner-gated computer use (desktop observation & actuation with a separate vision model, approvals, and a kill switch); multi-agent orchestration owner-gated

pillars.title: Automation pillar
pillars.summary: Zero code yet — research and blueprints are complete (n8n-pattern workflows, scheduler design, pre-identified traps). The audit scoped a concrete MVP in Track 4.

principles: Local-first — all processing on-device; LLMs are the only cloud hop
Additive architecture — no rewrites, every round layers on top of the prior
Quality over speed — every round is lint + typecheck + test + build + license-audit green
Approval-gated — the human approval engine IS the security boundary in v1
Honest status — the dashboard reports what is true, including failures
Documentation is a deliverable — ADRs, runbooks, and round-notes are required, not optional

audit.method: Five-agent audit fleet: four parallel domain audits (agent core & tools · autonomy & orchestration · workspace & project UX · platform & spec gaps) plus a synthesis pass producing the benchmark and roadmap. Every claim was verified against the actual source tree — file-and-line evidence, not doc claims.
audit.vision: The review target, in the owner's words: a full-fledged system that works autonomously, supports different kinds of projects, is highly customized for different tasks, does research and file changes, has full-fledged automations, and can continue or revert sessions.

headline.verdict: The three near-parity dimensions — sub-agent orchestration, background autonomy, approval design — are precisely the architecture's core bets, and they are validated. Every major deficit (automation 0/5, ecosystem 0/5, research 1/5) is additive work on a sound foundation, not re-architecture.

benchmark.verdict: Single exact-match edit path with before/after snapshots; no whitespace-to-elision fallback ladder, no reflection retries — fragile on imperfect matches.
Trim-only (oldest-pair drop); no auto-compaction, no cross-session memory — the memory policy field is stored but never read.
Genuinely good local-first base: turns survive disconnects, web push with the window closed, retry-from-event-log. But failed main sessions are terminal and there are no budgets.
Verified parallel delegation, key pools, semaphores, live monitoring — the architecture's strongest bet. Missing worktree isolation and per-role tool limits.
Zero code — research and blueprints only. Cline ships cron agents; OpenHands runs a dedicated automation server.
Snapshot blobs and a working restore endpoint exist — with zero frontend callers. One UI round away from parity on the backend.
Per-project rules files auto-load, but no project kinds, no per-project settings, and agent personas are silently discarded in project sessions.
Web search is Wikipedia-only; the browser is user-facing, not agent-driven; no vision despite the schema being ready.
One-shot commands, 60s cap, no PTY, dev servers blocked. The layered approval tiering is the redeeming design.
No MCP client, no plugins, no skills system — the single biggest ecosystem gap.
The fail-closed layered engine is the field's best design — undermined by web tools bypassing it, keys inherited by child processes, and an uncontained auto tier.
17 tools and a symbol index can walk there eventually; no token-budgeted repo map, and the prompt suppresses parallel tool calls the SDK already supports.

capabilities.note: SSE deltas, interleaved tool calls, thinking blocks, turn-grouped Working sections, per-reply usage chips, context meter, per-send model picker, file-path pills.
Up to 400 tool round-trips per message (outer loop × turns), path-contained file tools, search, git read trio, todo, web, index, delegation — every tool sandboxed to the project root.
5 roles, parallel dispatch with atomic semaphores, per-key API pools, live event forwarding, retry-from-event-log recovery, monitoring panel.
In-app center + SSE + desktop notifications + Web Push to a closed window (VAPID), click-through navigation, unread badge.
Symbol index (files + symbols in ~124ms on the demo), summary injected every turn, ⌘K palette with symbol/file/content modes and grep options.

Three wire formats (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Responses), custom providers, key pools, model listing + connection probe, per-agent and per-message model routing. R43: typed 46-entry catalog (18 free, default glm-5.2:free) + Free-only/All filter + provider-side free-model fallback chain.
5-step setup wizard with live connection test, 5 themes × light/dark, density control, demo mode.

Layered fail-closed engine live (blocked → destructive → auto → rule → ask, compound-command guard, 120s timeout). Holes: web tools bypass it, auto tier uncontained, keys leak to child processes, denylist not configurable, no audit viewer.

Event-sourced append-only log, resume any session with full history, background completion, explicit stop, restart-safe sweep. R43: failed turns persist turn.error and return to queued with a Retry card. Still missing: search, fork, export, list capped at 8 per project.
Every write/edit/delete snapshotted before+after; restore endpoint implemented and tested — but no frontend caller. Binary files corrupt on restore; no turn-level revert.
Projects are pinned folders with chat. No kinds, no per-project settings, no rename/recolor (no PATCH route), single default color for every project.

web_fetch is solid (real fetch, HTML-to-text, caps). web_search is Wikipedia-only — not a general search engine. Agent-driven browsing arrived in R43 (browser_control: navigate/back/forward/reload/set_viewport/get_state); click/type automation and vision still pending.
Honest one-shot runner (60s, output caps, history recall) for the user; agent commands approval-gated. No PTY, no long-running processes, dev servers blocked.
Budget-aware trimming with markers and a context meter. No summarization/compaction, no sticky context, no cross-session memory.
memoryPolicy and skills are stored, validated, editable in the UI — and never read by the runtime. Every session starts blind to prior sessions.
No scheduler, triggers, or workflows. Research + blueprints complete; MVP scoped in Track 4.
Only single-agent mode is accepted at session creation. auto-team and manual exist as types, not code. No shared bus, no task board.
No MCP client. The tool surface is a fixed set of 17.
Runs as a dev launcher + source tree. Desktop bundler disabled, no versioned installer, no changelog — the Rust shell compiles again (fixed in R43; CI green), so packaging is unblocked.

gaps.p0_intro: Broken or false today. These erode trust and two of them are security holes that must close before any autonomous work is built on top. All are small fixes — one dense round.
gaps.p1_intro: Directly unlock the owner's stated vision: continuing sessions, reverting, different kinds of projects, research, and the first steps toward autonomy.
gaps.p2_intro: Important for depth and the long game — MCP, vision, packaging, and the polish debt the audits catalogued.

p0.title: Rust shell failed to compile — CI red for 4 straight rounds (FIXED in R43)
p0.why: A Tauri API mismatch in the embedded-browser code broke the desktop shell build in R39; the last four CI runs all failed while this dashboard claimed green. R43 found TWO real API misuses (user_data_dir renamed data_directory in Tauri 2; on_navigation is a builder method), fixed both, and watched the runs to success via the API.

p0.title: Status reporting was false-green
p0.why: The dashboard and internal status file hand-claimed CI success, 243 tests, and stale milestones while CI was red and 262 tests were green. This rebuild makes it honest; the durable fix is auto-syncing CI status from the GitHub API at build time. (Since R43 this dashboard bakes its CI status from the GitHub Actions API at build time.)

p0.title: Provider keys leak to child processes (FIXED in R45)
p0.why: Approved commands inherit the full environment including provider API keys — any executed script or dependency can read them. Must be scrubbed before autonomy work. R45 closed it: every spawned child gets an ALLOWLIST environment (buildChildEnv at all six spawn sites) — a live child probe prints nulls for every secret-bearing variable.

p0.title: Auto-approved commands are not path-contained (FIXED in R45)
p0.why: The read-only auto tier (list/cat/grep/find) can touch any file on the machine, and auto-run build tools execute arbitrary project scripts. File tools are contained; commands are not. R45 closed it: the auto tier is now contained to the project root — outside-root, home-relative, parent-escape, and other-drive paths demote the command to the ask tier (cat /etc/passwd asks now); explicit always-allow rules still win.

p0.title: Web tools bypass the approval engine (FIXED in R45)
p0.why: web_fetch and web_search make ungated outbound calls with arbitrary URLs — an exfiltration channel for prompt-injected content. The spec requires every outbound call to be gated. R45 closed it: fetches and agent-driven navigation pass a host gate — a default documentation/source allowlist plus per-project always-allow host rules with the same interactive approval commands use; search stays friction-free but queries are secret-scrubbed first.

p0.title: The app database lives inside the source folder
p0.why: Re-downloading or cleaning the app folder destroys all sessions and settings. Needs a data directory outside the tree, pre-migration backups, and full export/import.

p0.title: Binary files corrupt on checkpoint restore
p0.why: Delete/write snapshots read files as text; restoring a deleted binary writes it back corrupted. Must fix before the revert UI ships on top of it.

p0.title: Dead navigation routes on the in-app dashboard
p0.why: Start-a-session and recent-activity buttons lead to an unrouted screen (404 placeholder); project rows drop the session id; one dialog links to another dead route. First-run credibility.

p0.title: Rot bundle: shutdown route, workflow YAML, stale docs
p0.why: The shell calls a shutdown endpoint that does not exist; a corrupted branch filter sits in both CI workflows; the canonical worklog stops at R37; the API truth doc under-reports ~20 live routes. (R43 refreshed the worklog and documented the browser/browser_control routes in the API truth doc.)

p1.title: Revert UI — the endpoint exists with zero callers (FIXED in R46)
p1.why: The owner's explicit 'revert to a previous session' ask: a restore endpoint was implemented and tested, but the frontend could only view diffs. R46 closed the UI half: every file-diff card carries a confirmed Restore action that reverts the file on disk (hidden for file creations, where the backend would delete the file); turn-level revert shipped in R44. The binary-safe restore dependency (P0-7) remains open.

p1.title: Failed main sessions are permanent dead ends
p1.why: Retry exists for sub-agents but not for the primary conversation — a provider crash mid-turn bricks the session. Generalize the proven retry pattern; also serialize concurrent turns (a latent interleave bug).

p1.title: Session search + uncapped list
p1.why: The sidebar caps at 8 sessions per project with a dead '+N more' link; there is no search. At 50+ sessions the product becomes unnavigable.

p1.title: Session fork — branch from any midpoint
p1.why: The event log makes forking a single copy-query: duplicate a session up to event N and explore a variant without losing the original. The experimentation workflow the owner described.

p1.title: Session export / import + markdown
p1.why: Zero backup or portability story today. JSON export of everything + per-session markdown transcripts.

p1.title: Memory system v1
p1.why: The spec's primary success criterion — remembering context between sessions — is unimplemented (the policy field is dead). Per-project markdown memory, injected per policy, editable in settings.

p1.title: Auto-compaction for long sessions (FIXED in R46)
p1.why: Trim-only context silently amputates the original task mid-run. R46 closed it the researched way: the over-budget head is summarized by the model into a dense briefing persisted as a session event (fork/revert inherit it, the summary is reused until the next overflow, round-2 compactions fold the old summary); a summarizer failure degrades to the old trim, so compaction never becomes a new failure mode.

p1.title: Project kinds + per-project settings
p1.why: The 'different kinds of projects' vision: research/writing/data/coding kinds with per-kind suggestions, tool defaults, and rules templates; plus a settings dialog (rename, color, default agent/model, approval-rule management) — there is no update route today.

p1.title: Persona merge + agent picker
p1.why: Agent system prompts are silently discarded in project sessions (replaced by the project prompt), so all five seeded agents are inert; the chat agent picker was removed with the old top bar and its store field is dead. Merge persona + environment prompts; restore the picker.

p1.title: Edit-reliability ladder
p1.why: The #1 agentic friction: edits fail outright on imperfect matches with no did-you-mean. The aider recipe — exact → whitespace-normalized → elision, structured errors with closest-candidate hints, up to 3 reflection retries.

p1.title: Real web search
p1.why: Research is bounded by Wikipedia. A pluggable search backend (Tavily / Brave / Exa) keyed like a provider, with the current engine as fallback. Needs the owner's API-key decision (Decision 1).

p1.title: Approval queue + remote approve
p1.why: Today an unattended agent waits 120s then is denied — not autonomy-ready. A persistent pending-approvals center plus Approve/Deny action buttons on push notifications turns the existing plumbing into a remote control surface.

p1.title: Cost tracking + budgets
p1.why: Recorded cost is always zero although the model pricing table exists; a runaway loop has no financial brake. Wire the estimate and add USD caps per run/day.

p1.title: Scheduler MVP (cron)
p1.why: The automation pillar's first real code: workflows + schedules tables, one sidecar loop, missed-run policy, manual-run-first. The n8n-pattern blueprint is already written and pre-audited for traps.

p1.title: Auto-team run mode
p1.why: The flagship multi-agent ask: a cheap orchestrator model planning and delegating to a powerful worker. Types exist; session creation rejects the mode. Needs approval queue + budgets first (P1-12/13).

p2.title: MCP client
p2.why: The industry-standard extension mechanism — every competitor supports it. Turns any MCP server into a tool; the biggest ecosystem unlock. After approval tiers extend to external tools.

p2.title: PTY terminal
p2.why: Long-running processes, dev servers, cd persistence, streamed output — an agent that builds but cannot run or verify its app is not autonomous.

p2.title: In-app file editing + diff review
p2.why: The file viewer is read-only today. Edit mode with snapshot-first saving keeps checkpoints consistent; open-at-line from chat and the palette.

p2.title: Worktree isolation for parallel sub-agents
p2.why: Five parallel agents mutate the same tree — last writer wins. Git worktrees per coding child with a user-approved promotion step.

p2.title: Per-role sub-agent tool limits
p2.why: Children currently get the full toolset minus delegation; a researcher can write files. Role-level allowlists are one settings layer.

p2.title: Vision / image input
p2.why: The vision-model field has existed since the first migration and nothing consumes it. Composer attachments → vision model; unlocks screenshot-driven UI verification later.

p2.title: Agent-driven browser automation
p2.why: The embedded browser is user-facing only. Navigate/click/type/screenshot tools feeding the vision model close the research loop.

p2.title: WebSocket event bus
p2.why: Two ad-hoc SSE channels today; the designed auth-framed gateway would unify streaming and unlock live automation UI. Design is already an approved ADR.

p2.title: Packaging & versioning
p2.why: Bundling is disabled, no installer, no changelog, no version discipline. Path: fix the Rust build → CI artifact (portable zip) → semver + changelog → launcher consumes releases. Depends on P0-1.

p2.title: Configurable denylist + approvals audit viewer
p2.why: The command denylist is hardcoded in source and always-allow rules are written but unmanageable. Two settings screens backed by existing storage.

p2.title: Skills system
p2.why: SKILL.md folders with progressive disclosure — the universal standard per the research corpus; the agent form already has a skills field that does nothing.

p2.title: Repo-map context economy
p2.why: Token-budgeted tree-sitter repo maps (the aider approach) are the long-term answer to multi-file awareness beyond the symbol index.

p2.title: QA & polish debt
p2.why: Zero Rust tests; the SSE stream route has no unit tests; palette lacks keyboard navigation; unreachable legacy layout code; one prompt rule suppresses parallel tool calls the SDK supports.

sequence.why: CI has been red for four straight rounds while the dashboard said green — the project's largest trust liability, and it's almost all S-effort fixes. The security holes must close before automation is built on top of them. Highest payoff-per-effort round in the plan; unblocks everything. — DELIVERED in R43: CI green + API-truthful dashboard; the security holes were deferred by the owner to a later round.
The owner's explicit vision sentence: continue a session, revert to a previous session. The backend largely exists — this is mostly surfacing work with immediately visible payoff.
The other explicit vision clause: different kinds of projects, highly customized. Independent of Track 2, so a clean round; gives R44's memory system concrete per-project hooks.

Edit ladder + real web search + PTY. Capability compounds: every later automation benefits from reliable edits and real research. Requires Decision 1 by this round. — DELIVERED in R46: context compaction + relevance-ranked memory + checkpoint restore UI + durable browser cookies + a provider-call timeout (a live-battery find); the edit-reliability ladder and in-app editing remain open.

Approval queue + remote approve + budgets. With gates closed (R43) and recovery solid (R44), overnight autonomy becomes safe; the queue turns existing push plumbing into the owner's remote-control surface. — R47 actually delivered the owner-directed provider-management round instead: one API layer, key+model-scoped connection tests, the served model catalog, enabled enforced at turn time, and the launcher key scrub; the approval queue, remote approve, and budgets remain open.

Scheduler MVP and auto-team, then the ecosystem bets in dependency order (MCP → packaging → vision). — R48 actually delivered the owner's Windows test-session fixes instead: sub-agent parity (approvals through the parent stream, codes, the live chat UI), the browser ticket flash-loop fix, the files explorer, sidebar polish, and the modern always-on-top folder picker; the scheduler MVP, auto-team, MCP, and vision bets remain open.

decisions.title: Search API provider + key
decisions.detail: Real web search needs one external API. Tavily (agent-optimized, free tier), Brave (privacy, free tier), or Exa/Serper.
decisions.recommend: Tavily free tier first — agent-optimized results, drop-in behind the existing tool; revisit if limits bite.

decisions.title: Gate the web tools?
decisions.detail: The audit strongly recommends routing web_fetch/web_search through the approval engine (fail-closed), optionally with per-domain allow rules later.
decisions.recommend: Yes — gate by default with an always-allow option per domain; aligns with the spec and closes the exfil channel.

decisions.title: Track order
decisions.detail: Confirm the R43–R48 sequence, or pull Automation earlier — accepting a scheduler landing before retry and budgets exist (a footgun the audits warn about).
decisions.recommend: Keep the proposed order; the foundation round is one dense round and de-risks everything after it.

decisions.title: Budget policy defaults
decisions.detail: Daily/monthly USD caps and breach behavior — hard-stop vs notify-only.
decisions.recommend: Start notify-only with a hard stop at a generous ceiling; tighten once real burn data exists.

decisions.title: Remote-approval surface
decisions.detail: Web Push action buttons (works from any phone browser, minimal build) vs a full mobile web app (much later).
decisions.recommend: Push action buttons now; a mobile app only if the button flow proves limiting.

decisions.title: Packaging timeline
decisions.detail: When does the dev launcher retire? Requires the fixed Rust build, bundler config, a content-security policy, and a changelog. Also makes the data-directory fix more urgent.
decisions.recommend: Fix the build in R43; aim for a first versioned portable zip as the Track 6 milestone, launcher retires after it proves stable.

decisions.title: Stay closed-source?
decisions.detail: The dashboard links only to this public repo; private-repo references are forbidden by its build scanner — the current behavior is correct for a closed-source product.
decisions.recommend: Stay closed-source; keep the dashboard as the public surface.

decisions.title: Initial project kinds
decisions.detail: Confirm Research / Writing / Data / Coding as the first four kinds, and whether user-defined custom kinds are in scope for v1.
decisions.recommend: Ship the four built-ins first; custom kinds after the per-project settings land and prove out.

features.title: The launch question (app or site, your choice every run)
features.desc: Since round 56 the launcher asks how you want to work before launching: [1] the packaged desktop app (the window with the embedded browser and the bundled engine) or [2] the site (local servers plus your browser — the launcher opens the address automatically). Enter keeps your last choice, the answer is remembered as the next default, and the app/site commands skip the question. When the desktop engine does not report ready, the launcher shows the engine's log tail and asks what to do next — retry the app, use the site instead, or keep the app — so a dead engine is never a dead end. The launcher's self-update now re-runs itself immediately (new launcher logic drives the very session it arrives in), the engine-watch timeout prints the engine's last output instead of going silent, and the status report names the remembered launch preference plus the engine's last successful boot.

features.title: Embedded browser
features.desc: A real Chromium browser inside the app: since round 50 every browser tab is a WebView2 child webview hosted in the main window — no proxy, no tickets, full CSS/JS, one shared profile so logins survive restarts — and since round 51 the desktop app itself installs in one click (the launcher downloads the CI-built NSIS installer, seeds the API keys into the Windows secure store, and launches it), so the native engine finally runs on the owner's machine with a visible engine badge and an automatic proxy fallback. The sidecar-proxy renderer remains the outside-the-shell fallback. Viewport presets 375→1920 + custom + zoom + rotate; the agent's browser_control tool shares the same state.

features.title: Right-sidebar tabs
features.desc: File viewer · Browser · Terminal · Sub-agents — a browser-style tab strip with per-session state and bounds-safe popovers; the Sub-agents panel renders phase cards (task → activity → files → report) with a live timeline and a failed banner + retry.

features.title: Notifications, everywhere
features.desc: Notification center with bell + unread badge, SSE stream, desktop notifications when hidden, and Web Push to a closed window via a service worker.

features.title: Sub-agent live streaming
features.desc: Multi-turn delegation with per-child sessions, live forwarded tokens (raw thinking + text streamed as they generate), the full live todo checklist, a centered stats footer (time, tokens up/down, tok/s, model), retry-from-event-log recovery, atomic concurrency slots, and per-provider key pools.

features.title: Approvals engine v1
features.desc: Layered policy (blocked → destructive → safelist → confirm), interactive Allow once / Always allow / Deny, 120s fail-closed timeout, compound-command guard.

features.title: Command palette ⌘K
features.desc: Symbol-search and file-open via Ctrl/Cmd-K with grep options (case-sensitive, whole-word, file glob, max results).

features.title: Project indexing
features.desc: Symbol index + index tool — 318 files / 2 384 symbols indexed in 124 ms on the demo battery; codebase summary injected into every turn.

features.title: Web tools
features.desc: web_fetch (real fetch, HTML-to-text, caps) + web_search — currently knowledge-search backed; the real search backend is Decision 1.

features.title: Streaming chat
features.desc: SSE text deltas + interleaved tool calls + thinking blocks + per-reply usage stats; turns complete in the background and notify when you're away. The composer carries permission modes, thinking levels, a provider→model flyout picker, and a context donut with main/sub-agent/combined session stats; the runtime guards against no-progress loops (nudge at 3 identical calls, honest stop at 5) and the prompt teaches understand-first, fewest-steps execution.

features.title: Background turns + stop
features.desc: Client disconnects no longer abort the turn — it completes, persists, and pushes a notification; an explicit stop endpoint returns a distinct aborted outcome.

features.title: Checkpoint snapshots
features.desc: Every write/edit/delete records before+after content; real unified diffs in the chat; 30-day retention. (The restore button arrives in Track 2.)

features.title: Per-project rules files
features.desc: Rules files in the project folder are auto-loaded into every turn's system prompt — a genuine agent-rules analog, file-based for now.

features.title: Free-model catalog + fallback chain
features.desc: 46-entry typed catalog (18 free models; default glm-5.2:free) after the old default died upstream. A persisted Free-only/All filter is shared by Settings, the chat picker, and the sub-agent picker; requests on free models carry a provider-side fallback (primary + openrouter/free) verified live through a 429 storm.

features.title: Sub-agent provider settings (temporary)
features.desc: A dedicated Settings tab (explicitly temporary): OpenRouter key slots isolated from the main key (pool slots 2–4) and a tool-capable, free-first sub-agent model override applied to every delegated child turn.

features.title: Failed-turn error cards + retry
features.desc: Failed turns persist a turn.error event (survives reload) and surface a live error card — model, reason, timestamp, Retry and Copy-details. Abnormal stream disconnects are detected client-side; a deliberate stop is never an error.

features.title: Chat geometry engine
features.desc: The chat panel fills its column at every width with a readable 1080px centered column and zero horizontal scrollbars from 700 to 2560px; the right sidebar yields smoothly below the 480px chat floor (the earlier cap regression removed).

features.title: Agent memory system
features.desc: Persistent per-project memory: memory_save / memory_recall / memory_list tools, a digest auto-injected into every turn's prompt (proved live: a no-tools turn recalled a saved decision), and a right-sidebar Memory tab with kind chips and delete.

features.title: Real web search
features.desc: web_search now queries the real web via DuckDuckGo (html + lite endpoints, ad/self-link filtering, uddg redirect unwrapping) with an honest MediaWiki fallback — live-verified in-turn with 8 real results.

features.title: Session search · fork · revert
features.desc: Full-text search across session titles AND chat history (?q=), one-click fork (copies the whole event log to a new top-level session), and revert-to-message with a confirm dialog (truncates the event log and appends a marker).

features.title: Streaming terminal
features.desc: The right-sidebar terminal streams stdout/stderr chunks live over SSE with heartbeats, a Stop button, exit-code footers (green/red), shrink-only timeout/output-cap overrides, and an automatic sync-route fallback.

features.title: Sub-agent keys auto-provisioned
features.desc: The launcher reads three optional sub-agent pool keys from its local credentials file (auto-appends them if missing), distributes them to the OS secure stores, and injects pool slots 2/3/4 — the Sub-agents settings tab shows them with zero manual pasting.

features.title: Security round: audit P0-3/4/5 closed
features.desc: Spawned children get an allowlist environment and never inherit the provider keys; auto-approved commands are contained to the project root (reading outside it now asks first); web fetches pass a host gate (default doc/source allowlist + per-project always-allow hosts, interactive approval) and search queries are secret-scrubbed before leaving the machine — each control live-verified through a real model turn.

features.title: Interactive terminal sessions
features.desc: Persistent shells per project: a real PTY engine (node-pty, pure-Node pipe fallback), a Run | Shell mode toggle with command history, live streaming with backlog replay for late viewers, idle reaping and per-project caps — shells never inherit secrets and never outlive the app.

features.title: Packaging v2: the installable desktop app
features.desc: The app version is single-sourced across all four manifests and gated in CI (0.51.0 today); a Keep-a-Changelog changelog spans 0.37→0.51. The release workflow now builds TWO artifacts on version tags: the CRLF-verified launcher kit, and — new in round 51 — a Windows NSIS installer (ACUTE-CODE_<v>_x64-setup.exe, per-user, no admin) bundling a pinned Node 24 runtime and the staged agent sidecar, proven bootable before shipping; the launcher installs it silently and seeds the owner's API keys into the Windows secure store.

features.title: Session manager reachable + mobile drawer
features.desc: The VLM verification pass found the session search/fork screen had shipped unrouted — unreachable at any size — and that phones had no navigation drawer at all (69px of content at 375px). Both fixed: the screen is live with sidebar navigation, and below desktop widths the sidebar is an overlay drawer (351px of content, auto-closing).

features.title: Context compaction
features.desc: Long sessions no longer silently drop their history: when the context window overflows, the model itself summarizes the over-budget part into a dense briefing (task, decisions, files, errors, open steps) that becomes part of the session — fork and revert keep working, the summary is reused until the next overflow, and a summarizer failure falls back to the old trim instead of failing the turn.

features.title: Relevance-ranked agent memory
features.desc: Memory recall now scores results by multi-token relevance (content-match strength, kind, importance and recency) instead of plain substring order; the digest injected into every turn ranks durable decisions above casual notes; and re-saving a known fact refreshes the existing memory instead of duplicating it — verified live through real model turns.

features.title: One-click file restore from checkpoints
features.desc: Every file-diff card now carries a Restore action (with confirmation) that reverts the file on disk to its pre-edit content — the restore backend existed since the first checkpoint system but had no UI caller for 21 rounds. A load-order race that could permanently hide the recorded snapshot on the first diff card was fixed along the way.

features.title: Browser cookies that survive restarts
features.desc: The embedded browser keeps cookies in the project database (parsed per the cookie spec, replayed and refreshed on every redirect hop), so logged-in sessions survive an app restart. Cookie values never reach logs, tool output, or the agent; cookies from the user's own browser can't be smuggled through; jars are kept per project profile.

features.title: One provider API layer
features.desc: All provider management — CRUD, API keys, key-pool slots, connection tests, per-provider model configs, the catalog — now lives in a single typed client layer every screen shares. The settings tab's private HTTP plumbing (a third parallel copy) and a dead legacy tab behind it were deleted in the same sweep. Disabling a provider genuinely stops its turns now: an honest 'enable it in Settings' refusal instead of quietly proceeding.

features.title: Key + model-scoped connection tests
features.desc: The connection test can target the primary key or any key-pool slot, optionally with a concrete model — a real one-token probe with measured latency instead of a bare reachability ping. Failures are reported as the provider sees them: an empty slot says so, a wrong key reads 'User not found', a throttled free model reports 429. Adding a pool slot no longer silently overwrites an occupied slot when earlier slots have gaps.

features.title: One served model catalog
features.desc: Every model picker — sub-agents, the agent form, the connection-test selector — now reads the backend's served catalog (46 models, free-first, tool and vision capability flags) instead of each screen keeping its own hand-copied list. New models appear everywhere at once; a deleted upstream model can no longer linger in one screen's stale copy. The agent form also lists custom providers and suggests known ids while still accepting free text.

features.title: Launcher ships zero key material
features.desc: The launcher template is a clean paste zone: two required lines, three clearly-optional sub-agent slots, every value a placeholder — the live keys it had shipped since round 44 are gone, and the launcher never writes key values. Scrubbing the baked-in defaults exposed and fixed a three-round-old parser bug that had silently ignored the owner's own pool-key values; a raw-key-reading API route with zero callers was removed in the same round.

features.title: Sub-agents at near-main-agent parity
features.desc: A sub-agent delegated from a live chat can now do what the main agent can: when it hits a needs-approval action (a non-read-only command, a web fetch outside the trusted hosts), it pauses and ASKS — the approval card appears in the parent chat labelled with the sub-agent's code and role, and the decision releases it. Every sub-agent carries a short code (like S23I) on the chat cards, the tab picker and its tab; the Delegated card lists each running child live and clicking one opens it; the sub-agent view is a real chat transcript — task, replies, tool calls with results, todo progress — with a per-second clock. Stopping the parent also stops its children; background retries still fail closed instead of hanging.

features.title: A real files explorer
features.desc: The Files action in the working sidebar opens a two-pane explorer: the project tree on the left (folders expand, files open on click, per-type icons) and the file's contents on the right — markdown rendered, code with line numbers and syntax colors, breadcrumb path. A Search button keeps the command-palette flow reachable, the tree collapses for narrow widths, and loading and error states are honest with retry.

features.title: The modern always-on-top folder picker
features.desc: Browsing for a project folder now opens the modern File-Explorer-style Windows picker — and it appears ON TOP of your windows instead of hiding behind them — both in the launcher/browser setup and in the desktop app. The old-style tree dialog remains only as a fallback if the modern one cannot load; both pickers fail honestly with an error line.

features.title: Background jobs — commands that outlive their tool call
features.desc: When run_command launches something detached (Windows `start /B`, Unix `&`, nohup), the call returns immediately with a job id and polling instructions instead of hanging on a pipe-holding grandchild — the exact 10-minute stall the owner reported. job_status lists/inspects every tracked job with its live output tail and log-file tail; job_stop kills it (process tree, process group, or command-line match); a hard watchdog tree-kills any command whose shell never exits within the timeout. The Terminal panel gained a Background-jobs view with live status and a Stop button per job.

features.title: Sub-agents are stoppable and supervised
features.desc: The Stop control now works on sub-agents exactly like the main agent — a Stop button on the sub-agent panel header aborts just that child, and the parent agent receives an honest 'sub-agent was stopped by the owner' report instead of a silent hang. While a child runs, a supervisor heartbeat streams what it is doing every 15 seconds (last activity, elapsed time, tool count, todo progress) into the panel, and a child with no activity for 5 minutes is auto-stopped and reported as stalled. Both thresholds are configurable in Settings.

features.title: The real in-app Usage screen
features.desc: The Usage page inside the app (previously a placeholder) is now a full analytics view over the local ledger: overview stat cards, a token activity chart with a 7/14/30/90-day range selector, a tool leaderboard with failure counts, model cards with token and cost splits, and a projects-to-sessions drill-down with sub-agent runs nested under their parents and click-through to each conversation.

features.title: A plugin-based tool system
features.desc: Every built-in tool group (filesystem, search, git, terminal, web, browser, memory, todo, delegation) is now a self-contained plugin module behind a registry — the tool catalog is computed from the real plugin declarations, so the app's tool list can never drift from the backend again. External tools ship as .mjs files dropped into ~/.acute/plugins (on by default) or the project's .acute/plugins (opt-in), with name rules, collision handling, and fail-soft loading.

features.title: Self-healing engine connection
features.desc: Since round 53 the app and its engine can never silently disagree: a branded splash holds the whole UI until agent-core is actually up (no screen can fire requests at a stale endpoint), the shell reports the REAL startup error when something breaks, a one-click Restart-engine re-runs the full lifecycle without an app restart, a watchdog notices mid-session deaths within ~20s and reconnects with a full data re-fetch, and every lifecycle line is written to sidecar.log for support. Root cause of the first-installer 'Could not reach agent-core' report — an ephemeral port persisted across launches plus a one-shot handshake race — fixed at every layer and pinned by regression tests.

features.title: Self-repairing installs + in-app engine diagnostics
features.desc: Since round 54 the launcher and the packaged app fix and explain themselves. The launcher verifies the install on DISK (app binary, pinned Node runtime, bundled engine) instead of trusting the Windows registry entry — which survives a manual folder deletion — so a deleted or half-written install is detected and REINSTALLED automatically, running copies are closed before upgrades so files are never replaced under a live app, and after launch the console watches the engine's own log and prints a plain 'engine is up — port' confirmation (or the failure log, right there). Inside the app, the engine's error channel is finally captured: its stderr is piped into the engine log, a failed start no longer leaves a zombie engine process holding the database (the real reason the restart button kept failing), cold boots retry three times before giving up, and the offline screen now shows the last log lines IN-APP with a one-click Copy-diagnostics button — any future failure explains itself on screen.

features.title: The engine-boot fix (EISDIR + the key namespace)
features.desc: Since round 55 the packaged engine actually boots. Tauri's resource_dir() on Windows returns \?-prefixed verbatim paths, and the shell handed them to the bundled Node as the program, the script argument, AND the working directory — Node starts from a verbatim program path but its module resolver cannot handle a verbatim entry script, dying with 'EISDIR: lstat C:' before running one line of engine code. Every packaged session since the first build showed 'Can't reach agent-core' while dev mode (plain paths) never saw it. All child paths are now stripped to plain Win32 form. The same round unified the credential namespace: reads and writes use the launcher's cmdkey targets (ACUTE-CODE/provider/<id>) so the seeded keys are finally found, with the pre-R55 keyring form kept as a read fallback.

features.title: The engine-bundling fix (the 189-junction link farm)
features.desc: Since round 57 the packaged engine's dependencies actually ship. The installer's bundled node_modules was staged by pnpm's default layout — a LINK FARM (measured: 189 symlinks on the build machine = 189 junctions after NSIS pack/extract) that Windows installers do not preserve — so the installed engine died with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND before its first log line, while every Linux-side check passed (Linux keeps links; the owner's disk did not). The staged tree is now a classic npm-style tree of REAL directories (301.5 MB → 124.6 MB), a zero-links gate fails the build if any symlink or junction appears anywhere in the tree that will be packed, and the release build now BOOTS the real staged engine with the real pinned Node runtime on a Windows runner — same command line, same environment, same ACUTE_READY handshake the app waits for — before the installer is ever built. The gate caught its own first two script bugs the same day it shipped; a dead engine can never be packed again.

features.title: Frameless window + integrated title bar
features.desc: Since round 58 the app looks like a full-fledged application, not a page in an OS frame: the native title bar (close/restore/minimize + app-name strip) is gone, replaced by a slim in-app bar — full-width drag region with double-click maximize, app identity at left, min/max/close at right, translucent over the shell's ambient background. Web mode unchanged.

features.title: Live file-write preview
features.desc: Since round 58 the agent's file writes stream LIVE: while the model is still generating the file's content, the working section renders a 'writing <file> — N chars' box with the partial content (tolerantly decoded from the streamed JSON), replaced by the final diff on completion. Battery-verified on the owner's exact 3-file task — 40+ content deltas stream during generation.

features.title: Honest stops + Continue
features.desc: Since round 58 stopping a turn is quiet and honest: a 'Stopped by user' card (no more 'generation failed / body stream buffer was aborted'), the sidebar spinner stops the moment you stop, the partial reply is kept, and a Continue button resumes the response from where it stopped. Sub-agent stops report 'stopped by the owner'.

features.title: Terminal chat harness
features.desc: Since round 58 whole agent sessions run from the command line: acute chat:stream renders live text/thinking/tool/approval output, Ctrl-C stops the turn (and exercises the real stop path), --auto-approve decides in-turn approvals, --raw emits JSONL for scripting. Long-session testing no longer needs the UI.

features.title: Settings restructure + visible keys
features.desc: Since round 58 Settings tells the truth: unconfigured preset providers sit in a collapsed 'Not configured' group; preset providers hide base-URL/API-format; the provider list sizes to its content; disable is a proper toggle with an agent-impact warning; Sub-agents and Advanced are two real pages; the chat picker honors hidden models and display names; and every stored API key — primary and pool slots — is one click away to reveal and copy.

features.title: The rounded window
features.desc: Since round 59 the desktop app paints a soft inset frame: 8px of breathing room on every side, the title bar and the content area as separate rounded cards, and window controls as inset rounded buttons (hovers never break the corners). The owner: 'make that top navigation bar rounded and give it padding on all four sides.'

features.title: Floating-pill scrollbars
features.desc: Since round 59 every scroll gutter in the app is minimal: a transparent track with a rounded pill thumb floating inset from the edges, visible in every theme and mode, vertical and horizontal, with a subtle hover state.

features.title: Pop-out browser with custom chrome
features.desc: Since round 59 the pop-out browser window has OUR chrome everywhere: a frameless window hosting a small dedicated app page (drag-region title bar with min/max/close, a themed editable URL bar, open-in-system-browser) with the page content in the same shared-profile embedded webview the in-app panel uses, sized to 70% of your monitor's work area.

features.title: Response ratings with full context
features.desc: Since round 59 every assistant reply carries thumbs up/down; bad ratings prompt an optional note; and the rating snapshots the complete evidence at the moment you rate it (your message, the reply with token usage, every tool event, any error). 'acute ratings --full' dumps the evidence for analysis so system prompts can be tuned on real failures.

features.title: Diagnostics console
features.desc: Since round 59 a right-sidebar Console tab shows every error the app knows about, newest-first with counts and expandable details: render crashes show an honest recovery card instead of a blank screen, and engine-side thrown errors land in the same view (secrets scrubbed, one click to copy or clear).

features.title: Modular system prompts
features.desc: Since round 59 every section of the agent's system prompt is a registry entry a project can override with a file — .acute/prompts/<section>.md replaces that section wholesale, an empty file removes it, _order.txt reorders. 'acute prompt:sections' lists them all. Without overrides the prompt is byte-identical to before.

features.title: Gutter scrollbar
features.desc: The pop-out window paints its own themed scrollbar OUTSIDE the content card — drag, click-to-jump, keyboard — tracking every page via the eval_with_callback scroll channel, with themed pills injected into every page and an honest single-bar fallback on CSP-strict sites.

features.title: Rounded browser view
features.desc: The pop-out's page content sits in a rounded, bordered card matching the title bar and URL bar — the owner-approved design language applied to the browser view itself.

features.title: Real browser zoom
features.desc: The embedded browser panel's zoom select now performs a true DPI-level page zoom (media queries and responsive layouts re-evaluate like a browser's Ctrl±) — previously it silently did nothing in native mode.

features.title: Title-bar sidebar toggle
features.desc: The sidebar's logo and collapse button are gone — the app's logo + name in the title bar now toggles the whole sidebar (hide for full-width content, click again to bring it back, present on every route).

features.title: Models, your way
features.desc: The models list starts empty — add exactly the models you want from the catalog picker (Free-only ↔ All-models toggle), then fully configure each one: pricing, context window, output limits, thinking, visibility.

features.title: Menus above the browser
features.desc: The right sidebar's new-tab menu now renders ABOVE the live browser preview — the native webview politely steps aside while a menu is open and returns when it closes, session intact.

features.title: Computer use
features.desc: The agent can observe and actuate the real desktop GUI: 30 tools — accessibility-tree-first element actions with screenshot-coordinate fallback, receipts-not-promises, fail-closed refusals, an enforced kill switch. Off by default; observe/act/autopilot postures; destructive actions need your approval in act mode.

features.title: A separate vision model
features.desc: Screenshots get described by the model YOU pick: a dedicated provider + model + its own API-key slot, configured completely independently — or the main model itself when its row is marked vision-capable.

features.title: Skills
features.desc: Add your own instruction modules (SKILL.md-style). Name + one-line description ride the system prompt; the agent loads the full body on demand when a task matches. The computer-use operating discipline ships as a built-in, editable skill.

features.title: MCP servers
features.desc: Wire in external tool servers over stdio MCP. Their tools join the agent's toolset as mcp__<server>__<tool>. Child environments are sanitized — no engine credentials ever reach a third-party server.

features.title: The computer monitor + mini window
features.desc: While the agent drives the desktop, a live monitor shows every step — what it's doing, what was refused and why, vision calls, running counts — in the right sidebar AND a floating draggable mini window with a STOP kill switch.

features.title: Sharper tool discipline
features.desc: The system prompts gained hard rules: read tool errors before reacting, pick the most specific tool, never fabricate results, report failures honestly, and close every task with what was done + what was verified.

features.title: A sidebar that minimizes
features.desc: The left sidebar collapses to a 64px icon rail (one click at its very top) — nav icons, your project tiles with live-running dots, notifications and settings stay reachable, and the full panel restores the same way. The state survives restarts.

features.title: The browser respects your dimensions
features.desc: Set a display size and the page actually renders at it: larger presets (a 1920×1080 layout in a side panel) scale down as a true view of the full-size page — the page sees the real CSS pixels, and the readout says exactly what renders, including the fit percentage.

features.title: Menus over the browser, finally
features.desc: The embedded browser is an OS-level layer, so app menus used to render underneath it. A DOM overlay watcher now hides the webview while any menu, dialog or popover is open — every UI surface paints above the page.

features.title: The agent uses your browser
features.desc: browser_control grew teeth: read a page's text, run JavaScript in the live page (click links, fill forms, extract DOM state), take a screenshot with a vision-model description, and list every open tab — all against the browser you watch live.

features.title: Settings changes land instantly
features.desc: Model and provider edits (renames, hides, prices, new models) reflect on the chat's model picker immediately; per-million input/output prices are clearly labeled with decimal support; partially-priced models now cost what their known sides cost.

features.title: A calmer, roomier layout
features.desc: The chat screen's gradient backdrop is gone — the three panels sit on the flat theme background with the side padding and rounded corners kept, so the workspace reads cleaner and the content gets the room.

features.title: The desktop app PROVES it's current
features.desc: The launcher now checks three versions on every launch — the registry, the exe on disk, and the running engine's /health — against the newest GitHub release, and a stale or half-replaced install is deleted completely and reinstalled from a sha256-verified download. ACUTE.bat reinstall / uninstall included.

features.title: Computer use actually sees your desktop
features.desc: The Windows backend's silent JSON array collapse is fixed (why list_apps came back empty), app enumeration now walks the REAL window list with process names, and app references resolve by title OR executable — an app_not_found refusal lists the running apps so the agent self-corrects in one step.

features.title: The always-on-top STOP bar
features.desc: A minimal floating monitor appears at the top of your screen the moment the agent starts using the computer — status, live activity, and a STOP kill switch floating above EVERY app, so you can halt it whenever something looks wrong. The right-sidebar computer tab is gone; one surface.

features.title: The surface boundary: embedded browser ≠ your desktop
features.desc: The agent's instructions now explicitly separate the two worlds — browser_control drives the in-app panel and can NEVER open your real Edge/Chrome or touch your desktop, while computer-use tools drive the real machine. The exact 'I opened Edge' hallucination from the first live run is now instruction-level forbidden, with honest narration required for both surfaces.

features.title: The auto-opening browser + debug mode
features.desc: The embedded browser tab now opens itself the moment the agent starts browsing (once per burst, scoped to that project — no more invisible browsing after an approval), and a new Debug mode switch (Settings → Advanced) makes every agent answer end with a raw execution report: each tool call, its outcome, what was verified — nothing hidden.

features.title: The agent drives the browser like a user
features.desc: browser_control grew to 15 actions: click elements by CSS selector or a button's visible label, type into inputs with the native value setter + input/change events (React and Vue pages actually register it) and real form submission, press Enter inside a form (native requestSubmit — the 'typed a Google query but never submitted' report), read a structured DOM outline, pull raw html/css/scripts, and run page JavaScript — the embedded panel is now a real working surface, not a viewport.

features.title: Bot walls the OWNER solves — a countdown card in chat
features.desc: When a page is blocked by a CAPTCHA, Cloudflare check, or age gate, the agent opens a live checkpoint card right in the chat: what kind of wall, the page URL, a draining 15-second countdown (60s hard cap), and two controls — Mark as done (the agent re-checks the page and continues) or Stop waiting (it reports back and asks how to proceed). Tool results carry the wall warning so the model calls it by itself.

features.title: A dedicated Image Analysis section + the analyze_image tool
features.desc: The vision model moved OUT of Computer Use into its own Settings → Image Analysis section: analysis mode, provider, model, and its own API-key slot (existing computer-use vision settings migrate automatically). It now serves computer-use screenshots, browser screenshots, and a general analyze_image tool (path or URL, ≤8 MB) that works WITHOUT computer use being enabled — with an honest refusal while off.

features.title: Debug mode: a post-turn, context-free execution analyst
features.desc: No more agent self-reports: after a completed turn, a FRESH model call with no tools receives the whole conversation transcript — every tool call's full result — and streams its execution report live in a dedicated section under the answer (structured report, tool trace, anomalies, verdict). It's persisted as a debug.report event that follow-up turns never see, so the analysis never pollutes the conversation.

features.title: Windows goes element-first in big apps
features.desc: The UIA accessibility walk now probes patterns only for the 17 interactive control kinds (one 4-probe pass — was up to 8 probes on every node) and reaches 2400 elements (was 800), and a new find_elements tool searches an app's tree by name or kind, returning indexed matches with bounds — the agent targets a specific control instead of looping on screenshots. The floating monitor shrank to a top-center 460×56 row, and browser turns never trip the 'agent is using your computer' indicator (live = decayed real-control events only).

features.title: One browser per chat session — instant navigation, no leaks
features.desc: The agent's embedded browser is now bound to the chat session that owns the turn (the agent tab's id IS the sidecar session id, bound before the turn starts): navigation travels as its own event frame and the sidebar creates the native web view the instant it lands — the blank-panel bug where a fresh tab never got a web view is gone. get_state reports only the addressed tab, background sessions never yank the visible one (the cross-session leak), cookie profiles are per-project, and the desktop sidebar's width snaps instantly so the web view never floats over the chat mid-animation.

features.title: The Windows bridge decodes WebView2's real eval dialect
features.desc: WebView2's ExecuteScriptAsync returns eval results JSON-encoded — and the in-page scripts already return JSON.stringify(...), so every callback string was double-encoded; the single parse yielded a string, and every click, type, eval, read_dom and source call failed with 'the page rejected the script' on real Windows (the harness mocks single-encode, which is why every test stayed green). The bridge now decodes both transports tolerantly, with honest errors for unexpected payloads — real-hardware browser automation works for the first time.

features.title: Chat image attachments actually upload
features.desc: 'I uploaded an image and the agent said it doesn't exist' is fixed end to end: dropped or pasted image bytes (up to 8 MB) now post to a dedicated authenticated upload route and land as real files at attachments/<name> inside the project — content-deduped (identical bytes reuse the file, conflicts mint -2/-3 suffixes, never an overwrite) — the message carries the project-relative path, and the model-facing history teaches the exact analyze_image call for that path. The OS file picker ingests binary picks the same way.

features.title: Live screenshot thumbnails while the agent thinks
features.desc: Every successful capture — computer-use screenshot, zoom, window state, and the browser screenshot action — now announces a frame to the open turn, and the chat renders a live thumbnail strip right under the working section while the agent is still thinking. Each tile lazy-fetches its PNG over an authenticated no-store route, and a click opens the full-size image with the capturing tool and timestamp. The rasters are deliberately ephemeral: an in-memory registry with a ten-minute lifetime, never persisted, never shown to the model — an expired tile says so honestly.

features.title: Debug reports you can copy — and a full-turn export
features.desc: The execution analyst's card now behaves: it expands while the analysis streams, collapses itself when done (folded reports stay minimized), and carries a Copy report button that always includes which model produced the report plus the full text — reachable even while the card is collapsed. With debug mode on, every assistant reply gains a second copy button exporting the whole turn as text: the thinking, every tool call with arguments and result summaries, approvals, and the final answer — capped at 100 KB with the tail kept.

features.title: Windows computer use, hardened for real hardware
features.desc: PowerShell scripts now ride EncodedCommand capsules through argv — no stdin pipe to lose and no exit-zero-with-no-output quirk ('the PowerShell session died before emitting JSON' is gone), with a Get-Process fallback when the window-enumeration probe stalls. The key tool maps real SendKeys chords from a key table — Tab is a keypress now, not the letters t-a-b, so the walk-a-form-with-Tab technique works — and the floating monitor holds through the agent's thinking gaps instead of vanishing after six idle seconds.

features.title: Every action returns an observation — the agent stops re-capturing
features.desc: The computer-use agent's 11 mutating tools (the clicks, scroll, type, key, set-value, select-text and drag actions) now attach an observation receipt to every result: a fresh frame id, whether the screen changed (a perceptual hash, not a guess), the focused element's name, and the frontmost app's title — read after a 600 ms settle. The verification the agent used to buy with a 5–25 second screenshot-and-vision round now rides the action itself, and the post-action frame renders inline in the chat at the moment it was captured.

features.title: Clicks verify what they hit — and the screenshot loop is refused
features.desc: Coordinate clicks upgrade from a blind 'unverified' to 'changed' or 'unchanged' via a perceptual pixel-diff of the frame before and after, and the hit-test the engine already ran now names the element the point landed on. Stale frames auto-refresh instead of dead-ending: an action on a frame older than 30 seconds re-captures and compares first — a static screen proceeds, a genuinely changed screen returns the already-registered fresh frame with zoom-then-retry guidance, and only set-value and raw left-mouse-down keep the hard refusal. A third consecutive near-identical capture with no intervening action is refused outright with three productive alternatives: act, wait, or find elements.

features.title: Real Windows input: SendInput typing, honest scroll, clipboard paste
features.desc: Keyboard input rides raw SendInput — per-character Unicode events and real virtual-key chords, including the win key; the deprecated SendKeys path that failed on modern .NET runtimes is gone entirely. The scroll tool was accidentally quadratic (it sent N wheel events each carrying N×120, so a 10-tick scroll moved 100× the intent); now one event carries the exact delta and horizontal scrolling rides a real hardware-wheel event instead of arrow-key taps that never scrolled page content. Typing over 300 characters rides a stdin-delivered clipboard paste, so the Windows command-line length ceiling no longer caps what can be typed into an editor.

features.title: Edge and Chrome elements, recognized by name
features.desc: Chromium only builds its web accessibility tree after an assistive technology pokes it — which is why element trees came back sparse. Every snapshot now pokes the render widget in both dialects (the MSAA and UIA object requests), polls up to two seconds for a cold tree, and freshly launched Edge or Chrome carries the renderer-accessibility flag so the tree exists from startup. Element searches return real links, buttons and inputs by name, element targets replace coordinate guessing, and middle-click and right-click take element targets now — open-in-new-tab flows without coordinate math.

features.title: The floating monitor: invisible to captures, never steals focus
features.desc: The 'Agent is using your computer' bar is now excluded from every screen-capture API: it renders fully on the physical display but never appears in the agent's own screenshots — which show what is behind it — so the vision model can no longer read the indicator text it used to 'detect'. It also no longer steals focus: re-opening the monitor no longer force-activates its window (the old call synthesized a stray ALT keystroke to grab the foreground — exactly the synthetic-input class the input rewrite eliminates), and the window is styled to never activate on click. The STOP button and dragging stay fully interactive.

features.title: Screenshots appear in chat at the moment they are taken
features.desc: Every capture — the agent's own screenshots, zooms and window states, plus the new automatic post-action observation frames — becomes a working entry pushed onto the live turn's stream at frame arrival, rendered inline between the tool rows as a compact click-to-enlarge tile exactly where it happened. The old bottom screenshot strip and its capped sidecar array are gone; tiles lazy-fetch their raster over an authenticated route and say so honestly when the ten-minute server lifetime has expired.

features.title: wait() reports what changed — frames are remembered perceptually
features.desc: The wait tool no longer returns an empty receipt: it reads the frontmost title before the sleep, then attaches the same compact observation afterward — a fresh frame, whether the screen changed, what is focused, and whether the app title flipped. After a navigation the agent waits and reads the change instead of screenshotting. Underneath it all, every registered frame carries a compact perceptual hash, so old-vs-new comparisons survive raster eviction and the spam guard judges near-identical captures without a vision round.

features.title: The agent knows its machine
features.desc: Every system prompt now states the actual OS + release, the real shell run_command spawns (cmd.exe on Windows, /bin/sh on POSIX), the current date, and the git branch + dirty state — a guarded 1.5s probe with honest fallbacks. The terminal section teaches only the real platform's syntax. Before R70 the model had to guess its own operating system.

features.title: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md auto-load — the cross-agent convention standard
features.desc: Project-root AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.override.md and CLAUDE.local.md are read every turn in a documented precedence ladder with source markers, and Claude-style @file imports resolve (relative, .md/.txt, 4 imports max, cycle-guarded). Every convention-rich repository opened in the workbench now has its instructions honored — the same standard Codex, Cursor, Cline and OpenHands read.

features.title: A real skills library: 8 built-ins + file-based skills
features.desc: Seven new built-in skills join computer-use — code-review, debugging, testing, git-workflow, web-research, project-init (the /init skill that analyzes a codebase and writes its AGENTS.md) and browser-use. Skills also load from files: .acute/skills/<name>/SKILL.md per project and ~/.agents/skills/ user-global (the Agent-Skills standard). Loaded skill bodies are STICKY — they survive history compaction instead of evaporating mid-task. Per-agent skill allowlists are wired (dead data since R61).

features.title: Verify before done — and never touch the user's work
features.desc: The prompt now teaches the completion loop top-tier agents run: after code edits, run the touched tests / typecheck / lint before claiming done (commands discovered from AGENTS.md or package.json; ask once, then remember). Dirty-worktree discipline: never revert or discard user changes, stop and report unexpected modifications, never git reset --hard. For 3+ file edits, an adversarial delegate review before reporting completion.

features.title: Errors at the END of logs finally reach the model
features.desc: run_command's 64KB output cap now keeps the head AND the tail with an honest middle-omission marker — build and test errors live at the end of long logs, and the tail was previously lost entirely. read_file returns cat -n line numbers with offset/limit pagination and honest empty-file messages; empty command output says '(no output — the command ran successfully and printed nothing)'. SWE-agent's finding: observation quality is model quality.

features.title: The prompt shrank 10% while teaching more
features.desc: Four overlapping sections that restated the same plan-batch-execute-verify posture four ways (agentic loop, efficiency, task planning, todo tracking) merged into one five-phase AGENTIC LOOP; the embedded-browser and computer-use sections were trimmed to essentials with pointers to the sticky skill bodies. 22,460 → 20,156 chars while adding environment grounding, conventions loading and verification discipline.

features.title: The prompt now teaches engineering discipline — with self-tests
features.desc: A new ENGINEERING DISCIPLINE section (2,312 chars, composed right after the agentic loop) carries the four karpathy principles, each with a binary self-test the model runs on its own diff — don't assume (present interpretations, never pick one silently), minimum code (nothing speculative), touch only what you must (clean up only your own orphans), define success criteria and loop until verified. [KNOWN]/[ASSUMED]/[UNKNOWN] tagging comes with 'NEVER write code that depends on an [UNKNOWN]'; a three-strike rule stops the 4th fix of the same shape; a red-flags table quotes the model's own rationalizations back at it ('I remember the file looking like this' → re-read it). Replies now end with verification receipts — the exact command + exit status, never a bare assertion — a 🟢/🟡/🔴 confidence tag, and one line of devil's advocate.

features.title: Failed tools escalate — the flail loop ends
features.desc: A per-session streak counter (the new edit-streak module) watches consecutive edit_file anchor failures and appends escalating recovery strategy after the honest base error: 2nd miss → re-read the file and copy the anchor EXACTLY; 3rd/4th → change your approach (read the region or write_file the whole file); 5th+ → refuse the pattern — and any success resets the streak. Truncation markers now carry the exact next call: read_file's >256KB marker states total line counts and 'use offset=N to continue', and oversized run_command output teaches the spill-to-file path (redirect to a file, then read_file it in slices). Owner denials are user feedback, not tool failures ('this is NOT a tool or system failure — ask why, or propose an alternative'), and timeouts are honestly distinguished from denials.

features.title: Six honest provider error classes — and overflow recovers
features.desc: Every provider/stream failure is now classified BEFORE it is flattened: context_window_exceeded / auth (by status only) / rate_limit / network / timeout / unknown, each with a class-specific honest message on the failure surface and the persisted turn error — a dead key no longer reads like a network blip (cline's veto: 'tokens exceeded' wording in a rate-limit body is a rate limit, never an overflow). The one class compaction can actually fix now recovers: a context-window rejection with nothing streamed yet emits the visible line '[context overflow → auto-compacted conversation → retrying]', force-compacts the conversation, and retries the turn ONCE — a second overflow lands in an honest terminal message instead of a fake success.

features.title: Twelve built-in skills with trigger-rich descriptions
features.desc: All 8 builtin skill descriptions were rewritten for the only reader that matters at trigger time — the model: 'Use when [verbatim phrasings]. [what it delivers]. NOT for [adjacent case].', quoting phrasings the user would actually say ('open Notepad', 'review this diff', 'my test fails', 'before I commit') so the model can choose between siblings instead of guessing. Four new discipline skills join them (12 total, INSERT OR IGNORE so existing installs converge): focused-fix (the Iron Law — NO FIXES WITHOUT COMPLETING SCOPE → TRACE → DIAGNOSE FIRST), zero-hallucination (evidence tags + the 6-rung YAGNI ladder), self-eval (the ambition × execution matrix — a claim without a receipt scores 0), and ship-gate (intercepts 'commit and push' / 'deploy' / 'ship it' with DO NOT SHIP / SHIP WITH NOTES / CLEAR verdicts).

features.title: The skill system reads your request — and says which skill matches
features.desc: A deterministic task→skill matcher (the new task-hints module — zero LLM, zero cost, per-turn) scores every enabled skill's description against the incoming message: quoted trigger phrases ('my test keeps failing, fix this bug') hit as case-insensitive substrings and score word-count × 5, stopword-filtered tokens add +1 each, anything qualifying at score ≥ 2 or a single phrase hit sorts to the top — two names max, contractions flattened on both sides so 'don't hallucinate' extracts as one phrase. The SKILLS prompt section then carries ONE advisory line after the list: 'Task signal: this request looks like it matches **debugging** — consider calling read_skill with that name FIRST' (with a parenthetical second match when there is one). Hints are computed per turn on both the sync and streamed paths from the same effective-skill list — a hint can never name a skill the model cannot load — and the golden prompt fixture stayed byte-identical: the line renders only when hints exist.

features.title: Eighteen built-in skills — the six crafts join the library
features.desc: tdd (NEVER WRITE THE TEST AFTER THE CODE TO FIT IT — 'a test you have not watched fail proves nothing'; minimum-to-green, triangulate, refactor only on green), api-design (THE CONTRACT IS WRITTEN BEFORE THE HANDLER — method+path+request+response+errors named first, one error envelope, additive-only evolution: 'a response that shifted is someone else's outage'), frontend-craft (STATE LIVES AS CLOSE TO ITS CONSUMERS AS POSSIBLE — semantic HTML, 'a click handler on a div is a bug', the a11y floor, stable-identity keys), typescript-craft (IF A STATE IS ILLEGAL, ITS TYPE MUST MAKE IT UNREPRESENTABLE — unions over flag soup, never-exhaustiveness, the any ban becomes unknown + narrowing, 'a cast is a confession'), security-review (the big five each with the exact test: injection → parameterized SQL, traversal → resolve + startsWith(root), secrets → the diff search before commit, authz → checked where the data is fetched, fail-closed → errors deny), and refactoring (NO MOVE WITHOUT A GREEN CHARACTERIZATION TEST FIRST — one mechanical move per step, a behavior change is a rewrite and gets named). Descriptions are trigger-rich with quoted phrasings ('write the test first', 'add an endpoint', 'fix the layout', 'is this safe', 'clean this up'); INSERT OR IGNORE converges existing installs on 18 while user edits persist.

features.title: Skills gain a second tier — references/ loaded on demand
features.desc: File skills in directory form can now carry a references/ subdirectory (the Agent-Skills standard): discovery is metadata-only — ≤8 .md files, byte-order sorted, sized, over-cap and hidden files skipped with honest logs — and read_skill's body output ends with the copy-pasteable listing 'references available: a, b — load with read_skill { name: …, reference: … }'. The new optional reference param loads one: the name is sanitized first (traversal rejected with the reason), the reference's own frontmatter is stripped at read time, and a 64KB cap trims with an honest '[reference truncated]' marker — never a silent cut. Database skills honestly report that they carry no reference files; the core-skills plugin manifest moved 1.1.0 → 1.2.0.

features.title: read_file carries the directory's own AGENTS.md rules
features.desc: The kilocode pattern, landed: reading a file inside a nested tree that carries its own AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md appends the deepest convention file's excerpt as a reminder — '--- [conventions from a/b/AGENTS.md apply to this file]' followed by a ≤2,000-char excerpt between end fences, so the directory's rules reach the model at the exact moment they matter. Injection happens once per session per source (an in-process dedup map — a restart re-injects once, harmless), the file content itself is returned unaffected, and the fences make even reading a convention file directly unambiguous.

features.title: Task modes — the posture layer: six built-in stances, customs in .acute/agents
features.desc: The division line from the modes module header: skills carry methodology, modes carry posture — a skill is instructions the agent READS, a mode is the stance it HOLDS for the class of task. Six built-in postures — plan, debug, build, review, explore, refactor — with bodies 2,084-2,546 chars each (iron laws, hypothesis discipline, honesty rules, escalation); the debug body is posture-pure, its method delegated to the paired skills post-verification. Custom modes load from .acute/agents/*.md: frontmatter name/description/tools, ≤8 files with 16K body / 500 description caps, 8 diagnostic kinds, and a custom shadows the builtin of the same id. resolveEffectiveModes — pure and synchronous, the skills-files pattern — returns the union for a project root, re-resolved every turn.

features.title: The mode surface — switch_mode, TaskModePicker, /mode, and the Task-signal line
features.desc: Three access paths, nothing auto-activates. Agent side — the switch_mode tool: called bare it returns the task-modes index with the active marker, activating returns the FULL posture guide exactly ONCE (a fenced task-mode reminder rides the turn), deactivating takes 'none'/'off'/'auto', and an unknown id gets an honest error listing every available id. User side — PATCH /sessions/:id activeMode (unknown → 400 with available ids, validate-before-write, no side-effect write), GET /projects/:id/modes (metadata-only, customs included), the composer's TaskModePicker (ModeSwitcher's mirror: the Compass trigger, menuitemradio rows, a custom-mode chip) and the /mode slash intercept (id-or-name, case-insensitive, word-boundary, local toasts). Between them the R72 matcher now scores mode descriptions too — quoted phrases ×5, tokens +1, top-2 — so the TASK MODES section carries an advisory 'Task signal … posture' line: a nudge, never a switch.

features.title: Twenty built-in skills — spec-planning and performance join the library
features.desc: The 18→20 round in the R72 house pattern (INSERT OR IGNORE, sortOrder 18/19): spec-planning — the decision-document methodology (context, constraints, options with explicit rejection reasons, the decision and its reversal trigger), written to pair with the plan mode — and performance — measure-first ('no optimization without a number to beat'), benchmark receipts, the change-one-thing rule. Descriptions 474/479 chars, trigger-rich in the house convention ('write a spec', 'make it faster'); bodies 1,898/1,895 chars with iron laws and pre-built output blocks. Loaded bodies stay STICKY across compaction and per-agent allowlists still gate read_skill, so the library's whole disclosure tier — description at trigger time, body on load — holds at twenty.

features.title: One system-reminder injector — byte-identical migration, per-turn budget
features.desc: The generalized engine the R72 design called for: the new system-reminders module (zero imports, pure) renders every fenced reminder through ONE function — renderReminder with a per-kind closing fence — plus a per-turn ReminderBudget (default 3) that keeps injected reminders bounded per turn. The proof of the migration: dir-conventions now delegates to the renderer and the pinned r72-dir-conventions suite stayed 20/20 green UNMODIFIED — the R72-d bytes unchanged. Consumers: conventions today, switch_mode's activation notice this round, the lessons-ledger next. Content policy stays at the call sites — the renderer is pure and dumb: no caps, no validation, no fs, no db.

features.title: The updater freeze, closed — the launcher picks the greatest version and names the tag it picked
