features.desc: Root-caused against the live GitHub API: the /releases list sorts never-published DRAFTS above every published release, so the five drafts the R63-R67 close-outs left behind sat at list positions 1-5, and the launcher's order-trusting first-match walk (unchanged since R63) returned the stale draft v0.67.0 as 'latest' — the installed 0.67.0 looked current while the newest published release was live, with no error anywhere ('it used to work' because in the all-drafts era list order was harmless). The fix — the first launcher change since R63, ACUTE.bat byte-identical with CRLF verified: the pure _pick_latest_release walks EVERY release and picks the numerically greatest version as integer tuples (0.10.0 > 0.9.0), keeps drafts first-class (the owner PAT sees them — a fresh draft installs on the next double-click), prefers published on same-version ties, and skips malformed entries without ever raising; _desktop_latest_release rides it at per_page 100 with one transient retry and the dev-flow fallback byte-identical. The freeze is now VISIBLE, not silent: the version-truth panel NAMES the tag it picked with its draft/published state, and ACUTE.bat status annotates it. Guarded by the repo's first Python suite — 10 stdlib-unittest tests covering the exact owner-freeze list shape (five drafts above published, asset id + digest passthrough), order immunity both directions, the lexicographic trap, the all-drafts era, tie-prefers-published, no-assets/empty, malformed-never-crash — wired into both the CI verify job and the release launcher-kit gate (every tag test-gated; the kit zip copies seven named files only). One-time remediation: the five stale drafts published (all HTTP 200, non-destructive), which un-freezes even a pre-fix launcher; the fix reaches the owner's own copy via the launcher's self-update (pull → copy + re-exec).

features.title: The transient-API retry ladder — the owner's schedule verbatim, six attempts, then an honest stop
features.desc: RETRY_LADDER_MS is the owner's schedule verbatim — [immediate, 1.5 min, 5 min, 10 min, 30 min], six attempts total, then stop + notify the user + show the error; rate_limit/network/timeout climb the ladder while auth/overflow/unknown NEVER auto-retry ('only for timeout or rate limit; other issues no auto-retry'). The wait is abort-aware — user Stop cuts a 30-min wait into an honest ABORTED, never a fake success — and ticks a 60 s SSE heartbeat so the UI stays live; the re-run re-enters the same outer-loop iteration, bounded, never infinite. The R71 six-class error classifier was extracted to a pure agents/error-classification.ts to serve it. THE DEEPEST FIND: the AI SDK delivers post-retry provider errors as fullStream ERROR PARTS which the adapter ignored — the runtime only ever saw a generic 'No output generated' → errorClass unknown → the ladder could never engage on a REAL rate limit; the adapter now re-throws the original error, live-verified against a mock 429 provider (meta.retry frames on the wire with the exact schedule). A NEW amber RetryStatusCard ('Retrying — attempt 2 of 6', the class chip, a live countdown, 'the agent keeps working automatically') appears during waits and is cleared by the first content frame; the terminal error card gains the class chip + 'after 6 attempts'; the task_failed notification body reports 'auto-retried 6 times (immediate, 1.5, 5, 10, 30 min)'. The same round closed four swallow bugs: the sync-path ok:true lie (a failed sub-agent used to report SUCCESS to the parent model — now an honest 502), the boot sweep's silent death (a sidecar crash mid-turn left the terminal failed with NOTHING in the timeline — now an INTERRUPTED turn.error event + queued, visible forever and retryable), errorClass + attempts now reach the frontend cards, and meta.overflow_recovery finally renders.

features.title: Hard task-mode enforcement — plan/review/explore read-only at the toolset, owner-pinned against escape
features.desc: The R73 modes were prompt-only — the toolset still carried write_file/edit_file/run_command, so 'in plan mode it made edits to files'. The NEW pure agents/mode-policy.ts INTERSECTS the turn's toolset: plan/review/explore collapse to READ-ONLY sets (plan = the R50 PLAN_MODE_TOOLS verbatim; review/explore add the git inspectors git_status/git_diff/git_log + analyze_image + job_status), debug keeps full tools but run_command demotes to the AUTO tier (ask-tier commands DENIED with an honest switch_mode note even under Full-Access), build/refactor full. The system prompt's toolNames matches the narrowed set exactly — the model never sees a write tool it cannot call; delegated children COPY the parent's activeMode so sub-agents cannot outrun the posture. READ-ONLY MODES ARE OWNER-PINNED: the first live e2e caught the model calling switch_mode('build') to ESCAPE plan mode — switch_mode now refuses to leave or clear plan/review/explore ('a read-only posture the OWNER set'). Live-verified: a plan-mode session asked to write a file honestly reported its read-only toolset and NO file was written. The mode menus are single-line with descriptions shown only on hover (native title tooltips) and accent 'read-only' badges on plan/review/explore; the mode bodies now state the ENFORCED fact, not just the wish.

features.title: The single-row composer and the 5-line textarea — the owner's exact order, no wrapping, real autogrow
features.desc: ONE row in the owner's exact order — attach, access, mode, context, model, reasoning, send ('one single row'): the composer box is a CSS @container and the selector pill labels hide below 560px (icon-only; the tooltips carry them) so the row fits at the 480px chat floor — measured 44px one-row at 386-641px where the old design wrapped to two rows below ~530px — with flex-wrap surviving as the never-overlap fallback. THE TEXTAREA NEVER AUTO-GREW, proven live: the old inline JS set height:132px while clientHeight stayed 34px, because the textarea's flex-1 made the flex algorithm IGNORE the height. Fixed: flex-1 removed, growth moved to a useLayoutEffect keyed on input (fires on typing AND programmatic fills — the suggestion-chip gap closed too), capping at exactly 5 visible lines derived from the live computed line-height: live-verified 3 lines → 73px, empty → 34px, 8 lines → 112px capped with internal scroll ('at least five lines, then scroll').

features.title: The composer's left/right split — send never wraps alone
features.desc: The owner's exact layout: attach, access level, and task mode on the LEFT; context donut, model, reasoning, and the send/stop action on the RIGHT. The right cluster is ONE nowrap group pinned right with ml-auto — previously flex-wrap could break the row anywhere and the send button dropped below ALONE, separated from its options ('the send message or stop message button was showing below the designated options'); now either the whole cluster fits on the row or the whole cluster wraps together. The model pill — the only toolbar control without an icon — leads with a Cpu glyph in the accent color that survives the 560px icon-only label-hide, and the @container one-row + 5-line autogrow from R75 carry through unchanged.

features.title: Failed sends stay visible — with the real API error
features.desc: The vanish bug behind 'I tried sending a message, but it was not that successful': a turn that failed BEFORE anything was persisted (a 400/401/409 rejection, a dropped stream) used to delete the whole session slice in cleanup — the error card flashed and disappeared, the user's message bubble vanished, and the transcript looked like the send never happened. The NEW stream-store freezeFailedTurn keeps the error card AND the typed message on screen until the next send; api.ts preserves the error envelope's real code + message + details (a 409 PROVIDER_DISABLED no longer masquerades as a generic provider error); and the TurnErrorCard's Show-full-error toggle expands the complete raw provider text instead of chopping at 220 chars. The waiting side was redesigned too (the amber retry card: a spinner chip, the six-dot attempt ladder with the breathing upcoming dot, a countdown fill-bar), and a whitespace-only zero-tool reply — the live battery's find — now fails honestly with a persisted NO_OUTPUT turn.error instead of completing ok while the requested edit silently never happened.

features.title: Revert-to-message is now edit-and-resend
features.desc: The owner's spec: 'it should revert to that session, and that message which was on that should be pasted in the message area. That message should be deleted from the chat itself with the agent.' The backend now truncates FROM the target message inclusive (the message is removed WITH its reply and every later turn — no dangling user message at the transcript's end), and the panel pastes the message's full text back into the composer and focuses it the moment the truncated transcript re-renders — the flow is edit-and-resend, not an orphan. The confirm dialog and toast say exactly that, and the model-facing history ends BEFORE the removed message, so the next send starts clean. Verified over the wire: revert → only the marker remains → status queued → a new turn works on the rebuilt log.

features.title: Honest errors — only a REAL rate limit shows as one; every other failure shows the API's actual text
features.desc: The owner's complaint: 'no matter the real cause, the UI always shows rate-limited'. Three defects, one fix each. The AI SDK's RetryError wrapper hid the real status code (the status walk never descended into lastError), so the genuine meta-router 429 classified by message-pattern LUCK — classification now unwraps the wrapper first (status walk over lastError/errors, depth ≤ 4, cycle-guarded), so a wrapped 429 classifies by STATUS. A 403 whose body says region/moderation/permission/unavailable used to report 'authentication failed' — a lie (the probe: a paid model on a free key returned 403 'This model is not available in your region' while the card said the key was rejected); such 403s now fail fast carrying the REAL text, while plain 403 stays auth and 401 stays status-only. userMessage was always a generic one-liner; it is now the provider's real words (trimmed, 240-char cap), the runtime's classMessage is the key-scrubbed real text, and providerError rides every meta.retry frame + both terminal error envelopes + the persisted turn.error. The live RetryStatusCard renders the class chip as the one-glance summary with the API's ACTUAL words beneath (mono, 3-line clamp, a Show-full toggle for long payloads). Live-pinned by the battery: a 400 model error, a 404 quota error, and a 403 region block all fail fast with the API's own words — only the account's REAL 429 ever ladders.

features.title: Send while the agent works — messages queue and auto-deliver with full context
features.desc: The owner's spec: 'While the agent is working, the user can still send messages; they queue and auto-send right after the current tool call; the agent reads them with full context and continues — never interrupting the in-flight flow.' A queued message is a session_events row of NEW type message.queued with the exact message.user payload, and delivery is a strict type FLIP on the same row — the message lands exactly where it was QUEUED (chronology is queue time; the model reads it at the next model call WITH the completed tool results). THREE delivery paths, one contract: loop-top delivery (the top of every outer-loop iteration, never spending loop budget; a message queued during a retry-ladder wait delivers at the rung boundary — the retry's prompt carries it); the turn-end same-stream continuation (meta.queue_continue, the first queued message consumed into the next FULL turn, the rest flipped to ride its history, capped at 25 continuations; Stop leaves the rest queued — never purged); and the pre-flip crash/stop recovery (lingering queued messages always deliver, in order, before the next send — a crash never loses them). The composer stays fully interactive while busy (the accent queue-send button beside Stop in the action anchor; Enter routes to the queue), amber chips render under the Working section (X-remove, 'Send now' when idle), delivered messages render as live user bubbles, and POST /sessions/:id/queue bridges a user.queued frame onto the OPEN stream — a 409 NO_LIVE_TURN falls through to a normal send. Verified by the request-body oracle: the queued text + the completed tool results appear together in the model's next prompt.

features.title: Auto-retry config in Settings → General — per-class switches
features.desc: The owner's ask: 'Add a retry-config section in General Settings — switches for auto-retry on timeout / rate limit.' Three switches — auto-retry rate limits (429), timeouts, network errors — all ON by default (the R75 ladder behavior out of the box: 6 attempts — immediate, 1.5 min, 5 min, 10 min, 30 min). The settings live server-side (GET/PUT /settings/retry, partial boolean patches with honest 400 validation) and the runtime reads them once per turn: the ladder gate is now PER CLASS in both turn paths, so a disabled class fails fast — attempts 1, no meta.retry frames, the provider's real error text on the card. The Settings tab formerly labeled 'Advanced' is now 'General' (the URL id and deep-links keep the advanced id — old links still work), with the Auto-retry card above Debug mode: per-switch partial PUT, an honest error line, and help text that tells the truth about the schedule ('when off, the failure shows immediately with the provider's real error text'). A toggle persists server-side — browser-verified with a GET round-trip.

features.title: The composer's never-wrapping action anchor — the bottom buttons never render in the wrong position
features.desc: The owner's report: 'The chat bottom buttons (Continue etc.) occasionally render in wrong positions.' The prior round pinned the send button to its right-side cluster, but the cluster lived INSIDE the wrapping toolbar row — when space ran out the whole group (Continue/Send included) could still wrap to the next line, landing below the designated options. The toolbar now restructures into a WRAPPING area (attach · access · task mode, then the donut/model/thinking selectors pinned right inside it) plus THE ANCHOR: a shrink-0 DOM SIBLING pinned right by the toolbar's justify-between — never inside any wrapping context — holding Continue · Send/Stop/queue-send, so the action button can never jump lines or drift. When the row gets tight the selector pills wrap as a unit under the left cluster while the button stays pinned bottom-right; the @max-[560px] label-hide and the left/right membership are preserved. Browser-verified stable at 386/480/560/641/900 px — the right gap is exactly the toolbar padding at every width, and at 386 px the selectors wrap INSIDE the wrap area while the actions stay anchored.

features.title: Addressable sub-agent tasks — the model's own handle (task_id) for every delegation
features.desc: delegate_task gained task_id: the parent model's own address for a delegation (grammar-checked, unique per session forever, duplicate-refused with the resume affordance). resume accepts the task_id, the child session id, or the 4-char code; the owner sees the address as a mono task-id chip in the Sub-agents panel and on the live sub-agent card (tooltip: delegate_task {"resume":"<id>"} collects it).

features.title: Background delegations — fire-and-forget runs that outlive the parent's turn
features.desc: background:true (with a task_id) returns IMMEDIATELY with a receipt while the child runs detached through the same machinery as blocking children — live status frames, notifications, the stall watchdog, the owner's Stop. A ~400 ms parent turn against a 4 s child, the child completing after the turn ended: the battery's S79-3 proof. The ≥10-outstanding cap refuses runaway fan-out honestly.

features.title: resume — the collect verb: waits, collects, retries, never polls
features.desc: resume on a running task WAITS (the call blocks until terminal — the R71 no-polling discipline's collection half: resume IS the wait); on a completed task it returns the final report idempotently; on a failed task it retries from where the child stopped (the event log is the resume point — a no-progress failure honestly re-sends). The parent turn's abort returns the honest 'still running' line.

features.title: The BACKGROUND TASKS reminder — the model is TOLD, never left polling
features.desc: Every turn, the system prompt lists the session's uncollected delegated tasks with live status (running 'Xm in, n/m todos' / COMPLETED — resume to read its final report / FAILED — resume to retry it from where it stopped). The section disappears once the report is collected (the delegation.collected lifecycle) and composes byte-identically for sessions without addressed children. The battery's request-body oracle proves the model actually SEES it.

features.title: The silent-stop guards — a chat can no longer just end
features.desc: The owner's report: "the chat ends without any error message or anything some times." Three root causes, three honest terminal paths: (1) a provider that closes the SSE stream CLEANLY mid-generation (no error, no finish signal) used to synthesize a finish — the turn "completed" with truncated text and no error; the truncation guard now detects content-without-a-finish-signal and throws the honest "connection closed mid-response" error, classified as a transient network failure so the auto-retry ladder can wait it out (the partial text is preserved). (2) The 800k-token context guard and the 200-request guard used to end the turn ok:true with SSE-only frames nobody rendered; they now fail honestly with CONTEXT_LIMIT / REQUEST_LIMIT codes, a persisted error, and an actionable message ("run /compact or start a new session" / "send a follow-up message to continue from where it stopped"). (3) A crash inside the stream route itself used to vanish on reload (nothing persisted, the session stuck running); it now persists the failure and fires the task-failed notification, best-effort and crash-guarded.

features.title: Raw provider errors — the real payload, verbatim
features.desc: The owner's ask: "for error messages raw messages should be shown too." Every error-detail cap that only ever hid the provider's real payload was raised — the persisted provider error detail 500 → 4000 chars, the user-facing one-liner 240 → 600, the connection-test and models-fetch surfaces 500/160 → 4000/2000 — while the UI's expand-toggle already collapses long text with a scrollable mono block. The API-key scrubbing discipline is unchanged everywhere, and the NVIDIA nvapi-… prefix joined the redaction surfaces. The connection test now shows the provider's actual body (a live NIM probe surfaces the real 410 "reached its end of life on 2026-08-26" message verbatim).

features.title: The customizable retry schedule
features.desc: The owner's ask: "in the settings retry customization is needed." Settings → General → Auto-retry now owns the whole schedule, not just the three per-failure-type switches: max attempts (2–10, default 6), the wait before each retry attempt (one editable input per rung, default 0/1.5/5/10/30 minutes), and the per-call provider timeout (60–3600 s, default 600). Every value is validated at the API and storage layers with the exact bounds the runtime resolves with; the schedule is resolved defensively per turn so a corrupt row can never break the ladder, and the defaults are byte-identical to the previous behavior. The task-failed notification's "auto-retried N times (…)" line and the card's footnote now phrase the schedule you actually configured — never a hardcoded one.

features.title: NVIDIA NIM as a built-in provider
features.desc: The owner's ask: "make sure it works with the nvidia api key too." nvidia is a seeded built-in provider (https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1, OpenAI-compatible — the chat-completions adapter speaks it as-is; models load through the existing /models fetch) with nvapi-… key support through the packaged app's secure key store and the dev sidecar's key file, a Settings Add-Provider preset, and the nvapi- prefix joined every key-scrub surface. Live-verified: the endpoint is reachable (198 ms), the 81-model catalog fetches, and the key authenticates; the account's NIM model functions have largely reached end-of-life server-side — the connection test shows those real provider bodies verbatim (the round's raw-error ask, incidentally proven).

features.title: One picker, three modes — Full Access / Ask / Plan
features.desc: The owner's directive: combine the six-builtin task-mode picker and the four-value access-level switcher into ONE selector. Full Access (all tools, zero permission asks — the agent decides how to work and switches postures itself as the task's shape changes), Ask (default: full tools, gates before important commands and changes), Plan (read-only — plan, read files, research, no edits or mutating commands; carries the full 19-tool read-only vocabulary with the retired review/explore extras folded in). The three descriptions are the owner's semantics verbatim, and the menu was browser-verified + VLM-passed: exactly three options, Ask marked default, no Editor, no task-mode pill, zero console errors.

features.title: Task modes became agent self-selected postures
features.desc: The six posture bodies (plan/debug/build/review/explore/refactor) and the .acute/agents custom modes survive as NON-ENFORCING guidance the agent picks via switch_mode — 'Discipline, not permission': the prompt sections read OPERATING POSTURES (self-select with switch_mode) and ACTIVE POSTURE, and the R75 enforcement tier (task-mode tool narrowing, the debug command tier, the read-only owner-pin) is retired — enforcement lives solely in the operating mode. The task-mode picker, the /mode slash command, and the modes query were deleted from the UI (AgentChatPanel 2,932 → 2,743 lines). Live-verified on a real provider: switch_mode persists a posture and the agent then works the read-only tools on its own recognizance.

A read-time remap covers un-migrated databases, old clients sending 'editor' get an honest 400 naming the mapping, and the modes feed keeps its readOnly flag always false for cached-client wire compatibility.

features.title: Custom-provider model routing — the misroute fixed at the wire
features.desc: The owner's report: custom models 'route through openrouter' and fail with unknown-model errors. The root cause was a wire-protocol omission — the composer's picker carried {model, providerId} but the send wire dropped the providerId, so the turn was prepared against the agent row's provider and a custom model id went verbatim to OpenRouter ('No endpoints found'). providerId now rides both send routes (with honest 400s for unknown ids), the queued-message carry, the vision relay, the context meter, and the debug analyst — a model picked under a custom gateway or NVIDIA serves THERE, with its own key; the sub-agent model setting takes the provider-scoped {providerId, modelId} pair and child turns provision their key pool from the effective provider. Live-verified with a mock-gateway oracle: a streamed turn with {model, providerId} lands on the provider's OWN endpoint with its OWN key.

features.title: The per-model Test button — a real completion probe
features.desc: The owner's report: 'when i test a model nothing happens.' Every configured model row (and the edit dialog) can now run a REAL minimal completion — max_tokens 16, a 30 s timeout, apiFormat-branched — with http/auth/model-accepted/non-empty-content checks, latency, a scrubbed reply preview (≤200 chars, the owner's eyeball-judge, deliberately not LLM-graded), provider-reported usage, and an honest failure reason. HTTP 200 either way: a probe that RAN and got a NO is a successful test call; no-key/no-row/dangling-provider get honest 409/404/409. Everything is double-scrubbed through the shared secret-shapes module — the R80 lesson structuralized into ONE scrubbing point (a hostile gateway echoing the bearer key back is scrubbed to 'bad key *** rejected').

features.title: Tri-state capabilities — unknown is no longer 'off'
features.desc: The owner's report: the model edit dialog 'behaves badly… there should be proper options for it like vision, audio, video.' Migration 0030 makes supports_tools/supports_audio/supports_video NULLABLE — NULL=unknown (the honest default for NIM/custom rows with no catalog source), 0=off, 1=on — and the INSERT path's old two-way ternary that folded an explicit null into false was fixed (the tri-state wire now records true/null/false exactly, pinned by its own suite). The edit dialog grew the capabilities card: Reasoning/Vision on-off toggles plus Tool use/Audio input/Video on-off-unknown tri-states, each with a consumed-by micro-hint and a Test-in-dialog button.

features.title: Custom-provider keys survive app restarts
features.desc: A key saved for a Settings-created provider used to work only in the session where it was saved — every restart ended in an honest-but-annoying 'no API key for provider' 409, because the shell's env-injection list was a hardcoded set of builtins. The shell now notes non-builtin provider ids at key-save time (ids only, never secrets — the round-61 vision note-file pattern) and re-injects each provider's env var into EVERY sidecar spawn, with the name derivation byte-identical to the sidecar keyring's (pinned by a unit test). Verified: cargo check and cargo check --tests both exit 0.

features.title: The honest context donut — measured beside projected
features.desc: The owner: 'the context, the token count — highly misleading.' The ring still fills with the estimate (its job is to move live during a turn), but every number is now labeled: '~N% projected · estimated' in the header, a NEW measured line carrying the provider's OWN prompt size for the last request (the actual block from the newest message.assistant stats carrier — 'not yet measured' before the first reply, never a fabricated 0, with ts + model riding along so a per-send model switch can't silently mix numbers), a compaction badge + an estimate that APPLIES the newest compaction (the ring visibly DROPS — the model receives summary + tail, not the raw log), the window-provenance note ('your override' / 'catalog default' / 'assumed 200k'), and the honest cache line ('— not reported by this provider'). The meter also builds the SAME prompt sections a real turn carries (skills, task-modes, the active mode, background tasks, environment) and MEASURES the real JSON tool schemas per tool instead of the fixed 350-tokens-per-tool guess. Live-battery-verified: actual=61 tokens measured end-to-end on a real OpenRouter turn.

features.title: ONE turn budget — the displayed number is the behavioral number
features.desc: resolveTurnBudget is now the single source every context number resolves through: contextWindow with its source label (override | catalog | default), maxOutputTokens from the models row (the owner's editable max_output_tokens column, finally READ after 79 rounds of being stored-and-ignored) → catalog → 32,768, margin 8,000, available = window − output − margin. The meter route, both turn runners, the compaction trigger, the context guard, and the compact route all resolve through it — the pre-R83 donut's 85% danger color and the compaction trigger disagreed on both numerator AND denominator; the donut now renders the same line as a budget tick + 'compaction line' note. Honest consequence, stated in the runbook: catalog models with huge declared output caps compact early — that is the truth of a shared input+output window, not a bug.

features.title: POST /sessions/:id/compact — the phantom /compact made real
features.desc: The pre-R83 context guard's error said 'run /compact' — a command that did not exist (and the hardcoded 800K limit fired BEFORE compaction could on big-window models). The affordance now EXISTS: POST /sessions/:id/compact force-runs the same assembleWithCompaction machinery with honest 404/409 gates (no agent / vanished agent / unconfigured model / missing provider / no baseUrl / disabled / no key), returning {compacted:true, throughSeq, droppedMessages, tokensSaved} or an honest {compacted:false, reason} — a single-message session declines (nothing to summarize), summarizer failure degrades to the hard trim, never a 500. The guard itself became model-relative (usedTokens > budget.available, the real limit in the meta.context_limit frame, the real numbers in the persisted error), and the summarizer's own spend is billed as an origin-'compaction' usage row.

features.title: Usage truth columns — provider calls, origins, honest billing
features.desc: Migration 0031 rebuilds usage_events (SQLite cannot ALTER a column constraint): provider_calls INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 (every pre-R83 row exactly true — one row per turn since R24), origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'turn' with its index, and agent_id relaxed to nullable for the hidden calls. The UI relabels 'requests' as Turns with the REAL provider-call count beside it (a 5-iteration turn is 1 turn · 5 calls — 'requests' previously meant three different things: turns since R24, SDK calls in the guard, steps in the AI SDK); the compaction summarizer and the debug analyst now record their own usage rows (origin 'compaction'/'debug' — hidden spend visible for the first time); the cache hit rate renders '— not reported by this provider' when no call reported a cache tier (NULL written, never a fabricated 0%); and model rollups carry costKnown, showing '(unpriced)' instead of a silent $0.00 free lunch.
